issues.legal_issue: General revenue-law procedures apply to proceedings under the land-reform law even when those proceedings arise under provisions outside the chapter specifically identified for limited procedural incorporation.
material_facts: The dispute arose from a suit seeking a declaration of landholding rights under a provision outside Chapter X of the land-reform law.
The land-reform law applied to the area and included a provision making the Land Revenue Act applicable to that area, subject to specified amendments.
Chapter IX of the Land Revenue Act addressed matters that were mostly not covered by the land-reform law.
issues.conclusion: The limitation in Section 293 to applications and proceedings under Chapter X does not restrict the broader application of the Land Revenue Act under Section 339(c); its relevant procedural provisions may apply to proceedings under other provisions of the land-reform law.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 293 and 339(c) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 must be read together. Section 293 limits the application of Chapters IX and X of the U.P. Land Revenue Act, 1901 to proceedings under Chapter X, while Section 339(c) has wider scope and makes the Land Revenue Act applicable to the area subject to the specified amendments. Sections 293 and 341 cannot curtail the width of Section 339(c). The Court overruled Sahdeo v. Deputy Director of Consolidation, Varanasi, which took a contrary view.

predicates.proceeding_under_land_reform_law: A proceeding was brought under the law governing land rights.
predicates.proceeding_outside_special_procedure_cha: The proceeding arose under a part of that law other than the chapter specifically identified for limited procedural incorporation.
predicates.governing_area_subject_to_general_revenu: The governing land-rights regime applied to the area and incorporated general revenue procedures, subject to specified modifications.

issues.definition: When a proceeding under the land-rights regime arises outside the specially identified procedural chapter in an area subject to general revenue procedures, those procedures apply to the proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A revenue appellate authority may refer a second appeal arising from a land-rights suit to arbitration when the general revenue-law procedure applies to the proceeding.
material_facts: A second appeal was pending before the revenue appellate authority from a decree in a suit seeking a declaration of landholding rights.
The parties jointly requested that the dispute be referred to arbitration.
The authority referred the dispute, an arbitrator made an award, and objections to the reference were rejected.
issues.conclusion: The revenue appellate authority had jurisdiction under Section 203 of the U.P. Land Revenue Act, 1901 to refer the dispute in the second appeal to arbitration.
issues.legal_principle: Section 203 of the U.P. Land Revenue Act, 1901 applied because Section 339(c) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 made the Land Revenue Act applicable to the area; Section 293 did not limit that broader application to Chapter X proceedings. Arbitration is a recognized mode of settling disputes, and the considerations supporting its use in proceedings under Chapter X apply equally to proceedings under other provisions of the land-reform law. The Court overruled Sahdeo v. Deputy Director of Consolidation, Varanasi, to the extent it supported a contrary construction.

predicates.second_appeal_pending_before_revenue_aut: A second appeal was pending before a revenue appellate authority.
predicates.dispute_arose_from_land_rights_suit: The dispute in the appeal arose from a suit concerning a claimed landholding right.
predicates.general_revenue_procedure_applies_to_pro: General revenue procedures applied to the proceeding under the governing land-rights regime.

issues.definition: If a revenue appellate authority has a second appeal arising from a landholding-rights suit and general revenue procedures apply, it may refer the dispute to arbitration.
